title: How payroll processing works
summary: The monthly payroll cycle from attendance cut-off to bank transfer and payslips.

p: Payroll starts with the number of days each person is paid for. Fix missing punches, approve pending leave and overtime, then treat the month's attendance as final.
Each employee's structure turns their fixed values into the month's figures. Earnings are usually reduced in proportion to paid days: earned = monthly amount × paid days ÷ days in the month.
Typical deductions are employee PF (12% of basic, commonly capped at ₹15,000), ESI (0.75% when gross is ₹21,000 or less), professional tax (state-specific), TDS and loan recovery.
Compare with last month, check new joiners and leavers, and get sign-off. A clear approval chain — HR, then Finance, then Management — catches mistakes before money moves.
Lock the run, create the bank file in your bank's format, upload it, then publish payslips. Statutory returns use the same locked figures.

title: How to manage employee attendance
summary: Setting clear rules for on-time, late, half day and absence — and applying them the same way every day.

p: Decide shift start and end, grace minutes, what counts as a half day and what happens when someone forgets to check out. Unwritten rules are applied differently by different people.
Registers are easy to fake. Face recognition at the entrance and check-in from a phone both record exact times and who marked them.
A quick daily look at absentees and late-comers prevents month-end surprises. Close the month on a fixed date so payroll can start.
Every edit should have a reason and a name attached. That protects both HR and employees.

title: Understanding salary components
summary: Basic, HRA, allowances, PF, ESI, PT and TDS explained in plain words.

p: Basic is the core fixed pay. HRA helps with rent. Special or other allowances make up the rest of gross. Some organisations also pay DA, conveyance or a fixed incentive.
PF, ESI, professional tax and TDS are taken from gross to get net pay. Loan instalments and advances are recovered here too.
Employer PF (12%) and employer ESI (3.25%) are paid on top of gross. They are part of CTC but not part of take-home pay.
CTC = gross + employer contributions (+ benefits). Gross = all earnings. Net = gross − employee deductions.

title: How leave accrual works
summary: Yearly versus monthly credit, carry forward and lapsing.

p: The full entitlement is added at the start of the year. Simple, but a new joiner may take leave they have not yet earned.
A fixed amount is added each month — for example 1.5 days for an 18-day yearly entitlement. Balances grow with service.
At year end, unused leave up to a cap moves forward; the rest lapses or is encashed according to policy.

title: How to calculate overtime
summary: Turning monthly salary into an hourly rate and paying extra hours correctly.

p: Hourly rate = monthly salary ÷ working days ÷ hours per day. ₹26,000 ÷ 26 ÷ 8 = ₹125.
Factory workers covered by the Factories Act get twice the ordinary rate. Others follow their policy or contract.
Only approved overtime hours should reach payroll, and the approval should be recorded.

title: What is a salary structure?
summary: How a structure turns fixed values into a correct monthly salary.

p: A structure is a list of earnings, deductions and totals. Some are entered per employee; others are formulas, like HRA = 40% of basic.
Different groups — teaching and non-teaching, staff and workers — often have different components and rounding. Each gets its own structure.
Before using a structure, try it with a sample salary and a short month to check proration and rounding.

title: How to manage shift scheduling
summary: Defining shifts, assigning them and keeping attendance rules in line.

p: Give each shift start and end times per weekday, breaks, grace time and weekly offs.
Most staff work the same shift most of the time. A default shift saves assigning everyone individually.
Temporary changes — a week on nights — are date-range assignments, so history stays correct.

title: Replacing the attendance register with face recognition
summary: What changes when staff check in by looking at a tablet instead of signing a book.

p: Registers record what people write, not when they arrived. Totals are added up by hand at month end.
A tablet at the entrance recognises each person and records the exact time. Late marks follow the shift automatically.
Mount the tablet at face height with steady light, enrol faces in the same place, and keep a PIN on enrolment so only authorised people can add faces.

title: A month-end payroll checklist for small HR teams
summary: Ten checks that catch most payroll mistakes before salaries go out.

p: Approve all leave and overtime. Add new joiners and record leavers. Apply any increments due this month.
Compare total net pay with last month and explain big differences. Check zero-salary and very high lines. Confirm bank details for new staff.
Get sign-off, lock the run, generate the bank file from the locked figures and keep a copy.

title: CTC vs in-hand salary: why the numbers differ
summary: A simple walk from CTC to the amount that reaches the bank account.

p: CTC includes employer PF and other employer costs that never reach the employee's account each month.
From gross, take away employee PF, ESI if applicable, professional tax and monthly TDS.
